title: Holonomic quantum gates via continuous measurement in bosonic codes: GKP and cat states
authors: Juan Garcia-Nila, Anirudh Lanka, Todd A. Brun
abstract: We apply continuous measurement-based holonomic quantum computation (CMHQC) to bosonic quantum error-correcting codes and develop explicit protocols for both four-component cat codes and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this framework, a continuously monitored time-dependent codespace undergoes a closed trajectory on the Grassmannian manifold while Zeno confinement suppresses departures from the instantaneous code subspace. For cat codes, we construct a family of squeezed-cat trajectories whose projected Wilczek-Zee connection generates arbitrary logical Z rotations, including non-Clifford T-gates. For GKP codes, we introduce a translated-lattice trajectory that realizes the logical GKP T gate through a purely geometric holonomy. We derive the corresponding time-dependent projectors, analytically evaluate the projected connections, and show that the resulting holonomies reproduce the desired logical operations without Hamiltonian control. Furthermore, we analyze the error-correcting capabilities of the instantaneous codespaces by establishing dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions for the relevant bosonic error models and derive analytical estimates for leakage induced by finite-strength continuous measurements. Our results provide a concrete realization of measurement-induced holonomic control in experimentally relevant bosonic platforms and establish a full fault-tolerant logical gate implementation.
summary: This paper details the use of Continuous Measurement-Based Holonomic Quantum Computation (CMHQC) to build robust logical gates on bosonic codes like cat and GKP states. By engineering time-dependent measurements, the authors show that the accumulated geometric phase realizes complex quantum gates without needing precise Hamiltonian control. This establishes a powerful theoretical pathway for fault-tolerant quantum computation in bosonic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation, specifically implementing non-Clifford logical gates (like the T gate), using measurement-based holonomic quantum computation.
main_result: They successfully develop protocols for both cat and GKP bosonic codes that demonstrate how continuous monitoring can induce geometric phases to realize desired logical operations without direct Hamiltonian control.
method: The core method involves applying Continuous Measurement-Based Holonomic Quantum Computation (CMHQC) by constructing time-dependent unitary paths on the code subspace, followed by rigorous error analysis using Lindblad master equations and Knill-Laflamme conditions.
model_or_system: The system utilizes bosonic quantum error-correcting codes, specifically focusing on four-component Schrödinger cat states and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states. The dynamics are governed by time-dependent unitaries that trace closed trajectories on the Grassmannian manifold.
key_observables: Fidelity of the implemented logical gate ($	ext{T}_L$), leakage probability ($1 - p_{	ext{code}}$), and the projected connection/holonomy around the code trajectory.
important_parameters: The measurement strength ($\kappa$) and the amplitude parameter $|\alpha|$ (for cat states) are crucial parameters determining fidelity and leakage bounds. The adiabatic limit is a key regime analyzed.
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting higher-order terms in the large cat state approximation ($|\alpha|^2 \gg 1$), and using Gaussian approximations for wave packet overlaps when calculating matrix elements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Wigner function snapshots showing unit fidelity during gate operation, plot process holonomy infidelity vs. code parameters (e.g., $|\alpha|$), and show the leakage probability decay as a function of measurement strength or time.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theory by first defining the CMHQC framework for bosonic codes, then deriving explicit protocols for cat and GKP states to generate logical gates, followed by detailed analytical calculations of error bounds (leakage) and gate fidelity using master equations and overlap integrals.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical blueprint for implementing universal quantum computation in platforms where continuous measurement is feasible, linking geometric phases directly to fault-tolerant logic operations.
